statement: At fixed Bessel argument, the mean-profile root strictly beats every other feasible point.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n S z t u : ℝ}  (hS : 0 < S)
    (ht : t ∈ Ioo 0 z) (hu : u ∈ Ioo 0 z)
    (hroot : n * (z ^ 2 - t ^ 2) = 2 * S * t) (hne : u ≠ t) :
    fixedArgument n S z u < fixedArgument n S z t
dossier_scope_note: The parameter-independent terms on that slice are omitted.

statement: On positive binary data, all interior shape log likelihoods lie below Poisson exactly at a nonpositive boundary score.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n S μ : ℝ} (hS : 0 < S) :
    (∀ w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, binaryGain n S μ w < 0) ↔ n*μ ≤ 2*S
dossier_scope_note: The general profile theorem below includes the positive-score branch.

statement: The variance of the polynomial degree is strictly below the barrier at every positive inverse argument for counts at least two.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) :
    degreeVariance k y <
      degreeMean k y * ((k : ℝ)^2-(degreeMean k y)^2) / ((k : ℝ)^2+(degreeMean k y)^2)
dossier_scope_note: The mean and variance are computed from the Bessel polynomial and its first two derivatives.

statement: The variance of the polynomial degree is strictly below the barrier at every positive inverse argument for counts at least two.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) :
    degreeVariance k y <
      degreeMean k y * ((k : ℝ)^2-(degreeMean k y)^2) / ((k : ℝ)^2+(degreeMean k y)^2)
dossier_scope_note: The mean and variance are computed from the Bessel polynomial and its first two derivatives.

statement: For every positive count, the log likelihood relative to Poisson is strictly concave in compact shape.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 < μ) :
    StrictConcaveOn ℝ (Ioo 0 1) (cellGain k μ)
dossier_scope_note: The result uses positive held mean.

statement: For a positive sample and positive held mean, the inward score determines the unique interior optimum or the strict Poisson supremum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℕ} {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 < μ)
    (hx : ∃ i, 0 < x i) :
    if 0 < inwardScore x μ then
      ∃! w, w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ IsMaxOn (sampleGain x μ) (Ioo 0 1) w
    else
      IsLUB ((sampleGain x μ) '' Ioo 0 1) 0 ∧
        ∀ w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, sampleGain x μ w < 0
dossier_scope_note: The log likelihood is measured relative to the Poisson value, so its boundary value is zero.

statement: The all-free finite maximum exists exactly when the sample variance exceeds the sample mean. It is unique when it exists. Otherwise the Poisson value at the sample mean is an unattained supremum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℕ} (hx : ∃ i, 0 < x i) :
    ((∃ p ∈ positiveChart, IsMaxOn (chartLogLik x) positiveChart p) ↔
      sampleMean x < sampleVariance x) ∧
    (sampleMean x < sampleVariance x →
      ∃! p, p ∈ positiveChart ∧ IsMaxOn (chartLogLik x) positiveChart p) ∧
    (sampleVariance x ≤ sampleMean x →
      IsLUB (chartLogLik x '' positiveChart) (poissonLogLik x (sampleMean x)) ∧
        ∀ p ∈ positiveChart, chartLogLik x p < poissonLogLik x (sampleMean x))
dossier_scope_note: The sample contains a positive count. The log likelihood drops the common factorial term.

statement: The Bessel argument and shape-to-mean ratio give a bijective chart on the positive parameter quadrant.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
:
    BijOn parameterChart (Ioi 0 ×ˢ Ioi 0) positiveChart
dossier_scope_note: The theorem identifies the domain used by the all-free result.

statement: At zero dispersion the rate is the geometric ratio S/(n+S), including rate zero.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ)
    {r : ℝ} (hr : r ∈ Ico 0 1) :
    IsMaxOn (fun q ↦ CMP.likelihood x q 0) (Ico 0 1) r ↔
      r = (∑ i, (x i : ℝ)) / (n + ∑ i, (x i : ℝ))

statement: At positive dispersion the model mean is strictly increasing in log rate.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{ν : ℝ} (hν : 0 < ν) :
    StrictMono (modelMean ν)
dossier_scope_note: The proof differentiates the summable moment series.

statement: The mean tends to zero as the log rate tends to minus infinity.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{ν : ℝ} (hν : 0 < ν) :
    Tendsto (modelMean ν) atBot (𝓝 0)

statement: The mean tends to infinity as the log rate tends to infinity.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{ν : ℝ} (hν : 0 < ν) :
    Tendsto (modelMean ν) atTop atTop
dossier_scope_note: The dispersion is held positive.

statement: The positive-dispersion CMP has one rate maximizer. It is zero on all-zero samples and matches the empirical mean otherwise.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ)
    {ν : ℝ} (hν : 0 < ν) :
    (∃! r, r ∈ Ici (0 : ℝ) ∧ IsMaxOn (fun q ↦ CMP.likelihood x q ν) (Ici 0) r) ∧
    ∀ r ∈ Ici (0 : ℝ), IsMaxOn (fun q ↦ CMP.likelihood x q ν) (Ici 0) r ↔
      (r = 0 ∧ ∀ i, x i = 0) ∨
        (0 < r ∧ modelMean ν (log r) = Discrete.avg x)
dossier_scope_note: The dispersion is held and the rate includes its atom at zero.

statement: A normalized exponential ray converges to the conditional weights on its exposed face.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{K : Type*} [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    (base slope : K → ℝ) (F : Finset K) (k : K)
    (hk : k ∈ F) (hzero : ∀ j ∈ F, slope j = 0)
    (hneg : ∀ j ∉ F, slope j < 0) :
    Tendsto (fun t ↦ rayMass base slope t k) atTop
      (𝓝 (exp (base k) / ∑ j ∈ F, exp (base j)))
dossier_scope_note: Uses finite support and the exposing signs.

statement: The normalized face product is the strict, unattained supremum along the ray.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{K : Type*} [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {n : ℕ}
    (hn : 0 < n) (base slope : K → ℝ) (F : Finset K) (x : Fin n → K)
    (hx : ∀ i, x i ∈ F) (hzero : ∀ j ∈ F, slope j = 0)
    (hneg : ∀ j ∉ F, slope j < 0) (hout : ∃ j, j ∉ F) :
    let u := ∏ i, exp (base (x i)) / ∑ j ∈ F, exp (base j)
    IsLUB (range (fun t ↦ ∏ i, rayMass base slope t (x i))) u ∧
      ∀ t, (∏ i, rayMass base slope t (x i)) < u
dossier_scope_note: The face weights are fixed and an excluded cell exists.

statement: At held size and interior probability, endpoint-only data have the exact strict endpoint-law supremum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{N n : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) (hn : 0 < n)
    (η : ℝ) (x : Fin n → Fin (N+1))

    IsLUB (range (likelihood x η)) u ∧ ∀ ν, likelihood x η ν < u
dossier_scope_note: The upper-to-lower odds on the face are exp(Nη).

statement: An interior empirical mean at positive size gives a unique finite log-odds optimum for held dispersion.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (ν m : ℝ)

    ∃! η, IsMaxOn (heldDispersionLogLik N ν m) univ η
dossier_scope_note: The objective is the per-observation parameter-dependent term.

statement: Two occupied adjacent cells at fixed size have the strict saturated face supremum at the empirical split.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{N n : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) (x : Fin n → Fin (N+1))
    {l u : Fin (N+1)} (hlu : u.val = l.val+1)
    (hx : ∀ i, x i = l ∨ x i = u)

dossier_scope_note: Size is at least two. Both free regular coefficients range over the interior probability chart.

statement: Both occupied endpoints at fixed size give the strict saturated endpoint supremum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{N n : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) (x : Fin n → Fin (N+1))
    (hx : ∀ i, x i = 0 ∨ x i = Fin.last N)
    (hz : 0 < multiplicity x 0) (ho : 0 < multiplicity x (Fin.last N)) :
    IsLUB (range (fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ likelihood x p.1 p.2))

        pairHeight (multiplicity x 0) (multiplicity x (Fin.last N))
dossier_scope_note: Size is at least two and the regular coefficients are free.

statement: An interior constant count has an unattained point-mass supremum at fixed size.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{N n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → Fin (N+1))
    {k : Fin (N+1)} (hk₀ : 0 < k.val) (hkN : k.val < N) (hx : ∀ i, x i = k) :

dossier_scope_note: Both regular coefficients are free.

statement: An odd held size and held interior probability give the central-pair face on data supported there.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{N n c : ℕ} (hN : N = 2*c+1) (hc : 0 < c)
    (hn : 0 < n) (η : ℝ) (x : Fin n → Fin (N+1))
    (hx : ∀ i, (x i).val = c ∨ (x i).val = c+1) :

dossier_scope_note: The upper-cell mass is the held probability, including when only the upper cell is observed.

statement: An even held size and held interior probability give the strict central point-mass supremum on the central singleton.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{N n c : ℕ} (hN : N = 2*c) (hc : 0 < c)
    (hn : 0 < n) (η : ℝ) (x : Fin n → Fin (N+1)) (hx : ∀ i, (x i).val = c) :

dossier_scope_note: The size is positive.

statement: Size zero gives likelihood one on the entire closed probability chart.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → Fin 1) (p ν : ℝ) :

dossier_scope_note: Every observation is necessarily the zero cell.

statement: At size one the exact likelihood is Bernoulli throughout the closed probability chart.
dossier_scope_note: The dispersion drops out of the law.

statement: At size one the probability maximizer is the empirical success fraction.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → Fin 2)

dossier_scope_note: This holds at any held dispersion and includes empirical endpoints.

statement: The fixed-size mean is strictly increasing in log odds for any held real dispersion.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (ν : ℝ) :

dossier_scope_note: Size is positive.

(N : ℕ) (ν : ℝ) :

dossier_scope_note: Holds for every finite size and real dispersion.

statement: With positive scale held and a constant cell observed, its midpoint strictly beats every other location.

{k B μ : ℝ} (hB : 0 < B) (hμ : μ ≠ k+1/2) :

statement: A cell whose closure contains the held mean has mass strictly increasing with inverse scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{k μ : ℝ} (hμ : μ ∈ Icc k (k+1)) :
    StrictMonoOn (fun B ↦ mass k B μ) (Ioi 0)
dossier_scope_note: The result is per cell.

statement: The cell directional information times mass is an integral of weighted squares.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{a b va vb : ℝ} (hab : a < b) :
    let p := intervalMass a b
    let s := intervalScore a b va vb
    let w := directionField a b va vb
    s^2*p + (b*kernel b*vb^2-a*kernel a*va^2) =
      ∫ z in a..b, ((s+z*w z)^2+(w z)^2)*kernel z
dossier_scope_note: The kernel is unnormalized. Affine endpoint velocities and an ordered interval are used.

statement: The cell directional information is strictly positive in every nonzero endpoint direction.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{a b va vb : ℝ} (hab : a < b)

    (intervalScore a b va vb)^2 +
      (b*kernel b*vb^2-a*kernel a*va^2)/intervalMass a b > 0
dossier_scope_note: The endpoints are finite and strictly ordered.

statement: The log mass of any cell is strictly concave in inverse-scale coordinates.

(k : ℝ) :

statement: Every nonempty sample has a strictly concave log likelihood in inverse-scale coordinates.

dossier_scope_note: No range condition is needed for concavity.

statement: A pair of observed cells with a positive separation gives a unique finite maximum.

{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℤ}

      ∀ p ∈ workingDomain, workingLikelihood x p < 1

statement: Two occupied adjacent cells have the strict, unattained Bernoulli supremum at the empirical proportions.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℤ} {k : ℤ}
    (hx : ∀ i, x i = k ∨ x i = k+1)

        (adjacentHeight (cellCount x k) (cellCount x (k+1))) ∧

dossier_scope_note: The face height is the product likelihood with the observed multiplicities.

statement: The discretized-normal maximum exists exactly when the integer range is at least two, and it is then unique.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℤ) :

      ∃ i j, x i+1 < x j) ∧
    ((∃ i j, x i+1 < x j) →
      ∃! p, p ∈ workingDomain ∧ IsMaxOn (workingLikelihood x) workingDomain p)
dossier_scope_note: Constant and adjacent cases are exhausted in the nonattainment direction.

hypotheses_and_conclusion: : BijOn workingChart workingDomain workingDomain

statement: At held rate the all-zero likelihood tends to one as shape decreases to zero and is strictly smaller at every finite positive shape.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :

statement: A positive count gives a finite shape maximizer at held positive rate.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℕ} (hx : ∃ i, 0 < x i) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :

hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) :

statement: At held rate a finite shape maximizer exists exactly when the nonempty sample has a positive count.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :

dossier_scope_note: Includes all-zero nonattainment and is independent of the curvature admission.

statement: The supplied pair is the unique maximizer on its singleton domain.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℕ) (a r : ℝ) :
    ∃! p : ℝ × ℝ, p ∈ ({(a,r)} : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) ∧

dossier_scope_note: The algebraic statement holds for any parameter pair.

statement: A positive count gives a unique finite shape maximizer at held positive rate.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℕ} (hx : ∃ i, 0 < x i) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
    ∃! a, a ∈ Ioi 0 ∧ IsMaxOn (fun b ↦ likelihood x b r) (Ioi 0) a
dossier_scope_note: Strict shape curvature follows from log-Gamma quantile spacing contraction.

statement: At fixed positive rate product, the stationary log ratio strictly beats every other ratio.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{z d t u : ℝ} (hz : 0 < z)

statement: For mean zero, unequal positive rates lose to equal rates at the same product in the fixed-product objective.

{z u : ℝ} (hz : 0 < z) (hu : u ≠ 0) :

statement: A continuous quadrant likelihood with a positive point and uniform vanishing tails attains.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{L : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ}

    {p : ℝ × ℝ} (hp : p ∈ Ici 0 ×ˢ Ici 0) (hpos : 0 < L p)

dossier_scope_note: The generic compactness step is instantiated by the Skellam sample theorem.

statement: Every signed Skellam atom is strictly positive at positive rates.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(k : ℤ) {p : ℝ × ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < p.1) (h₂ : 0 < p.2) :

statement: Skellam masses are continuous throughout the closed rate quadrant.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (k : ℤ) : ContinuousOn (mass k) domain
dossier_scope_note: The statement includes both axes and the origin.

statement: Poisson atoms vanish uniformly over their order when rate tends to infinity.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ R : ℝ, ∀ r > R, 0 ≤ r → ∀ j, poissonMass r j < ε
dossier_scope_note: This supplies the tail estimate for each convolution factor.

statement: For a nonempty sample the Skellam likelihood is uniformly small when either rate is sufficiently large.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℤ)

    ∃ R : ℝ, ∀ q ∈ domain, (R < q.1 ∨ R < q.2) → likelihood x q < ε
dossier_scope_note: The sample likelihood is a finite product of convolution masses.

statement: Every nonempty signed integer sample has a Skellam maximum on the closed quadrant.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℤ) :
    ∃ p ∈ domain, IsMaxOn (likelihood x) domain p
dossier_scope_note: The conclusion allows a zero rate.

statement: A mean-zero sample with one positive magnitude and both signs has exactly one maximizer.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℤ}
    {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (hx : ∀ i, x i = (k : ℤ) ∨ x i = -(k : ℤ))

dossier_scope_note: Both signs exclude the axes. The proof reduces to the equal-rate line.

statement: A Laplace score with a single positive-to-negative crossing is strictly negative after a zero.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{g : ℝ → ℝ} {c δ : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (hleft : ∀ t ∈ Ioo 0 c, g t < 0) (hright : ∀ t > c, 0 < g t)
    (hg : IntegrableOn g (Ioi 0))
    (ht : IntegrableOn (fun t ↦ exp (-δ*t) * g t) (Ioi 0))
    (hzero : ∫ t in Ioi 0, g t = 0) :
    (∫ t in Ioi 0, exp (-δ*t) * g t) < 0
dossier_scope_note: Uses integrability and strict sign on an interval.

statement: A Laplace score with a single positive-to-negative crossing is strictly negative after a zero.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{g : ℝ → ℝ} {c δ : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (hleft : ∀ t ∈ Ioo 0 c, g t < 0) (hright : ∀ t > c, 0 < g t)
    (hg : IntegrableOn g (Ioi 0))
